description:
AWS on Thursday launched Kiro bots, generally available within Kiro Crew, its open-source multi-agent development environment, to help developers coordinate parallel coding tasks, maintain context across sessions, and automate recurring software development workflows.

Kiro bots are designed to take responsibility for specific parts of a developer’s workflow rather than execute isolated tasks within individual agent sessions, in turn addressing the growing coordination burden developers face as they increasingly rely on multiple AI agents to handle software development tasks in parallel, AWS said in a statement.
title: AWS launches Kiro bots to help devs coordinate AI coding agents

description:
Meta has acquired AI coding startup Conductor, gaining technology that coordinates work across competing AI coding agents as it seeks a bigger role in software development tools.

Conductor announced the move on Wednesday, saying it would wind down its existing product while developing a new interface that it plans to introduce in early 2027. The company did not disclose financial terms or provide details about how its technology would be incorporated into Meta’s offerings.

Launched in July 2025, Conductor provides a platform that allows developers to run multiple AI coding agents simultaneously.
title: Meta acquires Conductor as AI coding shifts toward multi-agent development

That question came up for me while building an LLM analytics tool on Snowflake Cortex for healthcare engagement and field-performance data.
